title: From a photo of sheet music to MIDI

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Take a picture of sheet music and get a file a computer can play. That's what Maestro does.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Antoine's fork connects a React upload page to a Spring backend and some external music conversion tools.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does an image become music?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In two stages. First an optical recognition step reads the score, a bit like OCR for notes. That produces an intermediate score representation, and from there the tools generate MIDI.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the app is mostly the glue between those steps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right: upload, recognize, convert, download. It's Java for the backend, TypeScript for the interface and some Python for the recognition side, and the upstream project is credited.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A nice way to make a long pipeline feel like one button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The full page lays out the components.
